biotools.name: LiftPose3D

metadata.abstract: © 2021, The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Nature America, Inc.Markerless three-dimensional (3D) pose estimation has become an indispensable tool for kinematic studies of laboratory animals. Most current methods recover 3D poses by multi-view triangulation of deep network-based two-dimensional (2D) pose estimates. However, triangulation requires multiple synchronized cameras and elaborate calibration protocols that hinder its widespread adoption in laboratory studies. Here we describe LiftPose3D, a deep network-based method that overcomes these barriers by reconstructing 3D poses from a single 2D camera view. We illustrate LiftPose3D’s versatility by applying it to multiple experimental systems using flies, mice, rats and macaques, and in circumstances where 3D triangulation is impractical or impossible. Our framework achieves accurate lifting for stereotypical and nonstereotypical behaviors from different camera angles. Thus, LiftPose3D permits high-quality 3D pose estimation in the absence of complex camera arrays and tedious calibration procedures and despite occluded body parts in freely behaving animals.
metadata.title: LiftPose3D, a deep learning-based approach for transforming two-dimensional to three-dimensional poses in laboratory animals
